items.headline: Nvidia's CEO resigned on Nov 12 with immediate effect; the CFO is interim CEO and the company reports quarterly results on Nov 17
items.why: The largest AI-chip supplier now reports its first quarter without its founder-CEO and with no permanent successor named, so the call will be judged as much on leadership and guidance credibility as on the numbers.

items.headline: Nvidia guided gross margin to about 74% this quarter and warned it could bottom at 71%-72% next quarter on higher memory costs
items.why: Memory prices are now eating into margins at the most profitable company in AI hardware, which means rising component costs are a real constraint on AI-infrastructure economics, not just a headline.

sources.title: The Motley Fool: Nvidia reports earnings on Nov. 17

items.headline: Chip stocks split in the week to Nov 13: Nvidia fell about 9.6% while AMD gained about 14.6% and Arista about 14.7%
items.why: Money moved from the single dominant AI-chip name toward alternatives and networking suppliers, a sign investors are pricing AI spending as spread across vendors rather than concentrated in one.

sources.title: Financial News: The Weekly Close, Wall Street climbs as chip stocks split

items.headline: Bitcoin fell to about $62,100 on Nov 14, its lowest since August and more than 20% below early October, as spot ETFs shed about $1.9B over seven sessions
items.why: Persistent ETF selling plus roughly $1.2B of forced long liquidations shows the move is driven by funds and leverage unwinding, not a single news shock, which makes a quick snap-back less certain.

sources.title: Yahoo Finance: Bitcoin falls below $68,000 as ETF outflows extend
KuCoin News: Bitcoin falls over 12% amid ETF outflows and rate hike fears

items.headline: Bitcoin trades near $65,000 on Nov 17 with the Fear and Greed Index at 12 (extreme fear) while markets price a December rate hike at about 91%
items.why: Crypto is trading as a rate-sensitive risk asset right now, so the Fed's December decision and the inflation data matter more to price than any crypto-specific news.

sources.title: CryptoTicker: Bitcoin near $65,000, Waller and the December rate bet

items.headline: October CPI came in hot: headline +0.4% vs 0.3% expected, core +0.3% vs 0.2%, and the 10-year Treasury yield jumped about 14 basis points to 5.00%
items.why: A second straight upside inflation surprise removes the case for waiting, pushing the Fed toward raising rates in December rather than cutting and tightening financial conditions for every risk asset.

items.headline: Fed futures now price a December 9 hike at roughly 87%-91% for 25 basis points, with a Fed governor saying a 50-basis-point move should be considered if core inflation stays near 0.3%
items.why: The debate has shifted from whether to hike to how much, and a larger move would extend the dollar and yield strength that has been hitting gold and crypto.

items.headline: US-Iran peace efforts are stalling, with 36 confirmed attacks on commercial ships around the Strait of Hormuz in October, the highest monthly total since the war began
items.why: Shipping attacks at a wartime high keep a risk premium in oil even as diplomacy fades, and higher energy prices feed straight back into the inflation problem the Fed is trying to contain.

sources.title: Rigzone: Crude fluctuates as Iran tensions persist

items.headline: Gold fell below $4,000 an ounce on Nov 11, trading near $3,983, as the dollar rose toward its strongest since April 2025 and rate-hike bets increased
items.why: Gold is being driven by real yields and the dollar rather than by safe-haven demand, so it is falling even with an active war, and further hawkish Fed signals are the main risk.

sources.title: Kitco: Gold falls below $4,000 as dollar surges, Fed hike bets rise

items.headline: Brent settled at $95.84 and WTI at $88.56 on Nov 13, a second weekly decline from a six-month high, as the IEA said the market will be in surplus this quarter for the first time since the war began
items.why: A forecast surplus and rising US inventories cap the upside even with Hormuz tensions, so oil needs a fresh supply disruption, not just rhetoric, to push back toward its recent high.

sources.title: Rigzone: Crude fluctuates as Iran tensions persist

items.headline: US stocks closed Nov 10 with the S&P 500 at 7,520.93 (-0.38%) and Nasdaq at 25,065.88 (-0.74%) after the CPI release, then recovered to finish the week of Nov 9-13 higher
items.why: The index absorbed a hot inflation print and a 10-year yield at 5% without breaking down, but the weekly-gain estimates differ widely between sources, so the rebound is unconfirmed until it holds through the next data releases.

items.headline: Bitcoin is below its 200-day average (near $73,200 earlier this month), with support at $63,879 then the Nov 15 low of $61,946, and resistance at $65,502 then $65,980
items.why: Price is stuck in a tight band under a broken long-term average, so a close below the $61,946 low would confirm further downside while reclaiming roughly $66,000 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

items.headline: Gold broke below $4,000 with resistance at $3,988 then $4,020 and support at $3,910 then $3,890; silver holds near $51.56 with support at $51.09
items.why: Gold losing the round-number $4,000 level turns it from support into resistance, so a failed retest would point to the $3,890-$3,910 zone while silver's relative stability is the first divergence to watch.
